title: Structured Logging
description: Learn structured logging practices for microservices to enable efficient searching and analysis.

data.text: Structured logging formats log messages as structured data (usually JSON) instead of plain text. Netflix, Uber, and LinkedIn all use structured logging because it enables powerful searching, filtering, and analysis across millions of log entries.

Plain text logs are hard to search and analyze. Structured logs use key-value pairs that can be indexed and queried. You can easily filter logs by user ID, request ID, or service name—impossible with plain text.

data.title: Logging Best Practices
items: Use JSON format for machine readability
Include correlation IDs to trace requests across services
Log at appropriate levels: DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR
Include context: user ID, request ID, service name, timestamp
Never log secrets, passwords, or PII

data.title: PII and Secrets
data.text: Never log passwords, credit card numbers, or personally identifiable information. Use field redaction or scrubbing before logs leave your service.

data.title: Example: Structured vs Unstructured Logging
data.code: Compare plain text logs with structured JSON logs.

# Unstructured (hard to search)
[2024-01-15 10:30:00] ERROR: Payment failed for user 123, order 456, amount 149.99

# Structured (easy to search and filter)
{
  "timestamp": "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z",
  "level": "error",
  "service": "payment-service",
  "message": "Payment failed",
  "userId": "user-123",
  "orderId": "ord-456",
  "amount": 149.99,
  "error": "Insufficient funds",
  "requestId": "req-abc123"
}

items.question: What log format should I use?
items.answer: JSON is the de facto standard for structured logging. Some use logfmt (key=value pairs). Choose based on your log aggregation tool.

items.question: How much should I log?
items.answer: Log errors and warnings always. Log INFO for significant events (user login, order created). Use DEBUG sparingly as it can impact performance.

items.question: What is log correlation?
items.answer: Log correlation links logs from different services for the same request. Use a correlation ID passed through all services and included in every log entry.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Structured logs enable powerful searching and analysis
Always include correlation IDs for request tracing
Use JSON format with appropriate log levels
data.takeaway: Structured logging is the foundation of microservices observability; implement it in every service.
